cards.text: Friend, David and his men have been on the road a while, and on the third day they finally make it home to Ziklag. You know that feeling when you walk in the door and all you want is your own chair? Well, while they were gone, the Amalekites raided the Negev and attacked Ziklag.

cards.question: The Amalekites hit Ziklag while David and his men were away. What did they do to the town?
The Amalekites killed everyone they found in Ziklag.

cards.text: David's men walk into town and see it all. The town is burned down, and their wives and sons and daughters have been taken captive.

cards.question: Homes burned and families gone. What do David and his men do?

answers.text: Weep until they have no strength left
Sit in silence for seven days
Chase the raiders that same hour

cards.question: Two of the captives are David's own wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and ___ the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

cards.text: Now David is greatly distressed. The soul of every man is grieving for his sons and daughters, and that grief is looking for somewhere to land.

cards.question: In all that grief, what do the people in David's camp start talking about?
His town is gone, his family is gone and his own men are turning on him. Where does David find strength?

cards.text: Then David turns to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech: "Bring me the ephod." No pep talk. No plan drawn in the dirt. First stop, the LORD.

cards.question: Abiathar brings David the ephod. What does David do next?
David asks the LORD, "Should I pursue these raiders? Will I overtake them?" What does the LORD tell him?

answers.text: Pursue and you will rescue the captives
Stay and rebuild your town first
Wait here and they will come back

cards.text: So David and his six hundred men take off and reach the Brook of Besor. They already walked three days to get home, and now it's a chase. Friend, my legs hurt just TELLING this.

cards.question: At the Brook of Besor, some of David's six hundred men are too exhausted to cross. How many?
David waits at the Brook of Besor until his exhausted men are ready to cross.

cards.text: Out in a field, David's men find an Egyptian and bring him to David. The man is in rough shape.

cards.question: What do David's men do with the Egyptian they found in the field?

answers.text: Tie him up as a spy

cards.text: A piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins, and he eats and is revived. I know that look, friend. That's me when somebody yells FRESH BATCH from across the bakery.

cards.question: Why was the Egyptian so weak when David's men found him?

answers.text: No food or water for three days
Wounded in the raid on Ziklag
Lost in the desert for weeks

cards.text: Once the Egyptian can sit up, David asks him, "To whom do you belong, and where are you from?"

cards.question: The Egyptian tells David he's a slave. Whose slave is he?
The Egyptian's master abandoned him three days ago. Why?

cards.text: He tells David they raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the territory of Judah and the Negev of Caleb, and then: "we burned down Ziklag." WE. Friend, you are telling that to the man who LIVES in Ziklag.
David doesn't flinch. He asks him, "Will you lead me to these raiders?"

cards.question: Before he'll lead David to the raiders, what does the Egyptian ask David to swear by God?

answers.text: Not to kill him or hand him over
To give him a share of the plunder
To send him safely home to Egypt

cards.text: So he leads David down, and there they are. The Amalekites, spread out over all the land.

cards.question: David finds the Amalekites spread out over all the land. What are they doing?

cards.text: And David strikes them down from twilight until the evening of the next day. That's not a battle, friend. That's a DOUBLE SHIFT.

cards.question: Not a single Amalekite gets away from David.
Four hundred young men escape on camels, and that's it. Of everything the Amalekites took, how much does David bring back?

cards.text: Nothing's missing, and that includes his two wives. His men drive the flocks and herds out ahead, calling out, "This is David's plunder!" Friend, that's not a march home. That's a PARADE.
Back at the Brook of Besor, the two hundred men who were too exhausted to follow come out to meet them, and David greets them. Sounds nice, right? Hold that thought.

cards.question: The wicked and worthless men who went into battle with David have a plan for the two hundred who stayed behind. What is it?

answers.text: Give them only their wives and children
Make them carry all the plunder home
Send them back to the Philistine army

cards.question: David calls those men "My brothers" and tells them they must not do this. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The LORD gave it and protected them
The two hundred are his own family
Saul would punish them for it

cards.question: So how does David say the plunder gets split between the fighters and the men who stayed with the supplies?
David's rule about sharing alike becomes a statute and ordinance for Israel.

cards.text: When David gets back to Ziklag, he doesn't stack all that plunder in a corner and admire it. He starts sending some of it out.

cards.question: David sends some of the plunder as "a gift for you from the plunder of the LORD's enemies." Who does he send it to?

answers.text: His friends the elders of Judah

cards.text: Then the gifts go out all over, to Bethel, Jattir, Hormah, Hebron and every place where David and his men had roamed. That's a LOT of boxes to pack, friend, and I say that as a professional. And that's where we'll leave it for now, because trust me, this story's not done.

findings.problem: The passage opens mid-thought ("On the third day" counts from David being sent back from the Philistine army in chapter 29). The opening card says only that David and his men "have been on the road a while." It never says where they were or why they were away.

rule.text: If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.
